scope: Nine responsibility reviews across agent, daemon, runtime, workspace, config, terminal and preview, considering production and tests together. Evidence files identify reviewed boundaries and relevant checks, not a new line-by-line audit. Board-specific directories, functions and mixed-file behavior remain excluded.

groups.scenario: Run in-memory daemon session tests with host provider, retry and persistence environment variables set.
groups.reason: Build a complete explicit fixture config once and override only scenario properties. Keep real environment resolution in production and configuration-reload tests. Reuse the fixture in completion and hub tests; no new production configuration abstraction.
validation: The host-environment regression failed before the change and passes now. Session, approval, completion, activation, resume and real daemon tests pass.

groups.scenario: Discover instructions, skills and files inside and outside a checkout; fail an assertion before normal cleanup.
groups.reason: Test-only filesystem ownership belongs to test_support, not production instructions. Use TempDir lifetime cleanup, preserving canonical non-repository roots even when /tmp has .git. Embedded-skill tests construct the embedded registry directly. Keep asynchronous tool/process fixture lifetimes and real filesystem discovery separate.
validation: Instruction/skill cases and all three real no-repository boundary cases pass. tempfile is already locked and is added only as a direct dev dependency; no custom cleanup framework.

groups.scenario: Retry pre-generation failures, exhaust the 5xx budget, retry 429 beyond it, cancel during backoff or at its ready deadline.
groups.reason: Retry classification and delay calculation already accept explicit inputs. Preserve production retry semantics, jitter and the no-durable-output-retry rule. Use Tokio test time at the existing async wait boundary; no injected production clock or virtualized real sockets.
validation: Five loop scenarios run with a paused clock. Mid-backoff cancellation verifies one attempt and exactly 50 ms of virtual time; the competing-ready test verifies cancellation priority.

groups.scenario: Start a core from a PTY host, exercise command inputs, then disconnect either input owner while retaining the other.
groups.reason: Create paired channels inside terminal-core and keep receiver fields internal. Daemon and ten core scenarios use that constructor, avoiding unrelated per-command assembly in every test. Retain every sender for the fixture lifetime. Keep the explicit core select loop, query priority, actual synchronized-update timer and PTY ownership.
validation: Core regressions and real terminald tests pass. The new test joins the core after either PTY or command disconnection while the other input remains alive. Isolated terminal and workspace-restore GUI checks verify the integrated binary.

groups.scenario: Receive unlink/relink bursts, reach a quiet period, receive another burst, close the source or drop the watch task.
groups.reason: The native watcher already separates path/content decisions from event delivery and pane-owned tasks. Keep that production boundary. Replace a constant-only assertion with deterministic GPUI executor tests of the real debounce loop, without a clock interface or OS watcher mock.
validation: Three new tests verify delayed single reloads, subsequent bursts and both cancellation paths. Existing path/content and stale receipt tests plus the WASM gate pass. Native notify delivery is not simulated by the virtual-clock tests.

groups.scenario: Queue writes during startup, encounter a failed writer, activate a worktree, and fail persistence before acknowledgement.
groups.reason: Writer startup, retained write errors and durable acknowledgements already have focused seams. Activation owns lifecycle locking, persistence before publication, and rollback; pulling these effects apart would obscure ordering. Keep real signal, process and filesystem checks. The SIGTERM test still uses a real 750 ms startup delay and is not a deterministic scheduler proof.
validation: Existing barrier-based startup ordering, injected write/flush failures, activation rollback and real crash/resume tests pass in the full gate.

groups.scenario: Time out a queued operation, disconnect one view consumer, reconnect to a replacement peer, and drain one runtime.
groups.reason: Request waiting, typed daemon outcomes, route retirement and connection recovery already have separate owners. Keep timeout distinct from cancellation and real transport errors distinct from daemon replies. Unit-test connectors only retry explicit stubs; process isolation tests retain real OS scheduling and child cleanup.
validation: Request lifecycle and route tests pass; default-profile stub-recovery recorder and daemon integration tests exercise actual socket/process behavior.

groups.scenario: Receive conflicting inventories, fail one inventory, attach only surviving sessions, and invalidate results after runtime reload.
groups.reason: RestoreCandidates handles selection, RestoreRuntimes owns inventory/attachment effects, and the model validates all identities before mutation. Preserve generation checks and fail-closed persistence readiness. Agent attachment remains asynchronous while terminal attachment has its existing acknowledgement; do not flatten the difference.
validation: Existing conflict and metadata tests, model validation/reconciliation tests and isolated UI restart preserving session IDs pass.

groups.scenario: Resolve defaults/file/environment, reject malformed reloads, expand grants against an explicit home, and translate provider settings.
groups.reason: Path selection, parsing, precedence and grant validation already have explicit value inputs; startup default fallback and reload failure intentionally differ. Preserve production env readers, accepted current-daemon versus startup-provider settings, and live grant revalidation. Only the daemon unit fixture stops invoking production config resolution.
validation: Existing path/precedence, malformed reload, provider translation/selection and grant tests pass. No production setting or permission is changed.
